# Hybrid Pi Dispatch: Pane When in a Herdr Session, Headless Fallback Otherwise

## Problem statement

The evaluation of Pi subprocess mechanisms (discovered-from:WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7) found that /skill:audit is dispatched two ways: user-initiated audits open a visible herdr pi pane via send-to-pi.sh, while automated contexts (heartbeat, cron, CI, ssh) must run headless via `pi -p --mode json`. Currently the choice of mechanism is hard-wired per caller and there is no shared way to get a visible pane when a herdr session exists and fall back to a headless subprocess when it does not. The podcast editor (open_source_llm/experimental/herdr-podcast-editor) already implements exactly this hybrid pattern via a HERDR_ENV check; it is a proven precedent to generalise.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want agent work to be visible whenever a herdr session is present, even when the invocation originates from a script or automated context.
- **Skills authors / plugin authors** — want a single reusable dispatch primitive instead of maintaining two mechanisms.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when an audit is triggered from a context that has a herdr session available, I want it to open in a visible pi pane so I can watch it."
- "As a producer, when no herdr session is available, I want the same invocation to fall back to headless execution so the work still happens."
- "As a plugin author, I want to dispatch a skill to pi once and have it choose pane-vs-headless automatically."

## Expected behaviour

- A shared dispatch helper determines at runtime whether a herdr session/pane environment is available (e.g. HERDR_ENV or herdr CLI/socket presence, mirroring the podcast editor).
- When available: dispatch via send-to-pi.sh (visible pane).
- When unavailable: fall back to `pi -p --mode json` headless execution with the same command.
- Existing callers keep their behaviour; new callers (e.g. heartbeat audits, user-initiated audits outside the worklist) opt in.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Add the helper to the shared herdr scripts (packages/herdr/shared/) and/or a small skill-level utility so both herdr code and skills can use it.
- Model the fallback on the podcast editor's send-to-pi.sh wrapper + direct-subprocess branch.
- Wire the heartbeat audit dispatch to use the hybrid helper (pane when herdr present, headless otherwise), which also delivers visibility (see WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A shared dispatch helper exists that selects pane vs headless at runtime based on herdr availability.
2. With a herdr environment present, dispatch opens a visible pi pane running the given command.
3. Without a herdr environment, dispatch runs the command headless via `pi -p --mode json` and returns programmatic output.
4. At least one existing caller (e.g. heartbeat audit dispatch) is converted to use the helper without regressing its current behaviour.
5. Tests cover both branches (herdr present / absent).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Problem

During the excessive-spawn investigation (WL-0MSB19J56006E87J) and in normal operation, `worklog.db-wal` grows large under concurrent writer load (16MB WAL observed). Worklog uses SQLite in WAL mode by design (`src/persistent-store.ts` sets `journal_mode = WAL` for concurrency).

Observations:

- Writes land in `worklog.db-wal` first; `worklog.db` mtime/size stays unchanged until a checkpoint merges the WAL back. A 66KB `worklog.db-wal` was observed in `open_source_llm/.worklog` while `worklog.db` sat untouched — and the WAL files disappear once all processes close (checkpoint on close / auto-checkpoint).
- Under the spawn storm (206 concurrent wl processes), the WAL reached ~16MB, meaning auto-checkpointing was not keeping up with write volume.

Why this matters:

1. **Read cost:** SQLite reads must scan the WAL, so a large WAL slows every read query.
2. **Cache invalidation:** mtime/size of `worklog.db` alone is unreliable while a large WAL holds live writes (see WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 AC #2 — cache must be WAL-aware).
3. **Crash/recovery:** a large WAL means longer recovery time on abnormal exit.

## Goals

- Understand current checkpointing behavior: default auto-checkpoint threshold, when/where wl checkpoints (per-write? on close? explicit wal_checkpoint?), and how concurrent writers interact.
- Determine whether a large-WAL state is a correctness risk or only a performance cost.
- Decide if wl should checkpoint after write batches (e.g., after `wl sync` or bulk mutations) or rely on auto-checkpoint.

## Suggested approach

- Inspect `src/persistent-store.ts` and `src/database.ts` for pragma settings and any checkpoint logic.
- Reproduce: run N concurrent write processes against one worklog and measure WAL growth, read latency, and checkpoint behavior.
- Consider adding an explicit `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE/TRUNCATE)` after write-heavy operations if evidence supports it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Documented understanding of when/where checkpointing happens and why a 16MB WAL occurred (root cause identified, reproduced, or ruled out).
2. Measured impact of large WAL on read latency (before/after numbers).
3. A recommendation recorded on this item: leave as-is, add explicit checkpointing, or tune auto-checkpoint threshold — with rationale and risk notes.
4. Any code change is tested and does not regress the full test suite.

# Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold

## Problem statement

When the herdr worklist selection list (`createListRenderer` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) has more work items than fit in the visible list area, the renderer silently trims the visible window to fit the pane height. There is no visual cue (scroll marker, count, ellipsis) that additional items exist below the fold, so users cannot tell the list is truncated and may miss items.

## Users

Anyone using the herdr worklist pane (`worklog-selection-list` plug) to browse/select work items, in particular with more items than fit on screen (the default list of 20+ items on smaller panes, or with the metadata panel reserving 20–40% of the height).

User story: *"As a herdr user, when the worklist pane shows more items than fit, I want to see a `▼ more` marker so I know the list continues below the fold and I can scroll (j/k) to see the rest."*

User story: *"As a herdr user who has scrolled down, I want to see an `▲ more` marker at the top of the list so I know there are items above the current viewport."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the flattened item list exceeds the visible list area at scroll offset 0, the rendered list output contains a dim-styled `▼ more` marker at the bottom of the items region (after the last visible item, before the footer/fill rows).
- When the list is scrolled down (scrollOffset > 0) with items above the viewport, the rendered output contains a dim-styled `▲ more` marker at the top of the items region (before the first visible item/group separator).
- When all items fit in the visible area (no overflow, scrollOffset = 0), no indicators are rendered.
- The `rows - 1` line-count invariant is preserved with indicators active: rendered output plus the notification line still fits the pane height (regression guard for WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).
- Indicators are non-selectable display-only rows: they do not consume navigation state, selection index, or hierarchy scroll offset (`getVisibleItems`, `_adjustScroll` semantics unchanged).
- New unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: indicator shown when items exist below the fold; `▲ more` shown when scrolled; no indicators when the list fits; line-count invariant with indicators active.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- Must preserve the `rows - 1` line-count invariant established in WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO (notification line always fits; header never scrolls off the top).
- Indicator wording is generic ("more"), not exact counts — group separator rows make exact "N more" counts unreliable.
- Scope is list mode only: the detail view and the metadata panel (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X) are unchanged.
- Match existing styling conventions: dim-styled (`ANSI.dim`), consistent with other non-interactive chrome (footer hints, filter bar).
- Indicator rows must be included in the render budget (the `visible` trimming loop and the fill-blank count) so output never exceeds the pane.

## Existing state

- `createListRenderer` sizes the visible window with `flatItems.slice(scrollOffset, scrollOffset + listHeight)` and trims it with `visible.slice(0, -1)` when items + group separators exceed `budgetForItemsAndSeps`. Nothing signals that trimming happened.
- The pane header shows `(top N of M)` only when the *fetch* was truncated (`totalCount > items.length`), not when the *display* is truncated by the viewport — so a full fetch with a small pane shows no cue at all.
- Scrolling works (j/k via `scrollOffset`, `_adjustScroll` keeps the selection visible), but at rest positions there is no indication of hidden items in either direction.
- The Pi TUI browse list (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts`) is a separate surface and already shows `(top N of M)` in its title; pi's built-in `SelectList` component renders a `(N/M)` scroll-info line when overflow exists — the established pattern this change mirrors.

## Desired change

- In `createListRenderer` (list mode), after the visible window is trimmed to fit:
  - Emit a dim `▼ more` line at the bottom of the items region when `scrollOffset + visible.length < flatItems.length` (items below the fold).
  - Emit a dim `▲ more` line at the top of the items region when `scrollOffset > 0` (items above the viewport).
  - Account for indicator rows in the budget: include them in the trimming calculation and in the fill-blank `used` count so the `rows - 1` invariant holds.
  - Edge case: if reserving the bottom indicator row trims the window so that `scrollOffset + visible.length == flatItems.length`, the bottom indicator is omitted (the list then fully fits); this must terminate in a single pass (no loop).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer`: compute indicator presence from `scrollOffset`/the trimmed visible window, emit `▼ more`/`▲ more` rows, and include them in the budget (`budgetForItemsAndSeps` trimming loop + fill-blank `used` count).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — add unit tests: indicator shown when items below fold; `▲ more` shown when scrolled; no indicators when list fits; line-count invariant with indicators active; indicators are non-selectable display rows.

## Related work

- [Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane (WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO)] — completed; established the `rows - 1` line-count invariant and the visible-window trimming logic this change extends.
- [Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X)] — completed; defines `listArea`/`panelHeight`, the fold boundary of the list region.
- [Create a work item selection list in Herdr (WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP)] — origin of the selection list.
- pi-tui `SelectList` component (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/components/select-list.js`) — reference pattern: `(N/M)` scroll-info line when the list overflows `maxVisible`.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: generic "more" wording is sufficient (user: "more" is fine); exact counts are intentionally avoided because group separators make them unreliable.
- Risk: indicator rows shrink the visible item window by up to 2 rows when overflow exists. Acceptable — the alternative (no indicator) is the bug being fixed.
- Risk: budget accounting bugs could regress the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO line-count invariant. Mitigation: the existing invariant tests plus new tests with indicators active cover both top and bottom indicators.
- Edge case: bottom indicator row reservation could trim the window to fully fit, making the indicator unnecessary — handle without looping.
- Scope-creep guard: the Pi TUI browse list also lacks a fold indicator, but it already shows `(top N of M)`; improving that surface is out of scope and could be tracked as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Indicator style — which do you prefer? (a) a footer line in the items region like `▼ N more` (dim), shown when items exist below the fold; (b) a position indicator like `(N/M)`; (c) both: `▼ N more` footer plus a `▲ N more` header when scrolled down" — Answer (user): "(c) Both". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Scope — should this cover only the list-mode pane (herdr worklist), or also the detail-view scroll indicator (which already exists via the metadata panel scroll)?" — Answer (user): "confirm" (list-mode only). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Count precision — exact remaining count (e.g. `▼ 5 more`) vs. a generic marker (e.g. `▼ more`)? Exact counts can be wrong when group separators consume rows." — Answer (user): "`more` is fine". Source: interactive reply.

- **WL-0MP15YJEQ000FVWS** – Documentation: colour mapping & fallbacks (completed)
- **WL-0MLRFF0771A8NAVW** – TUI: prevent mouse click-through from dialogs to underlying widgets (completed)
- **WL-0MLOS7X1C1P82B5J** – Append no-questions instruction to OpenCode prompt (completed)

# Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ)

## Problem statement

The Herdr work item selection list (`packages/herdr` TUI) is keyboard-only. Users of Herdr — a mouse-first, terminal workspace manager — cannot click or tap a work item to select it, cannot use the mouse wheel or touch gestures to scroll the list, and the detail/filter views are unreachable without keys. This makes the selection list feel foreign inside Herdr's pointer-friendly environment and unusable on touch-first devices (tablets, touch laptops).

## Users

- **Herdr users** who expect a pointer-driven experience: click/tap to pick an item, wheel/touch-scroll to browse.
- **Touch-device users** (tablets, touch laptops, convertible terminals) who have no usable keyboard navigation path — touch taps and drags must work.
- **Human reviewers/auditors** who switch between many work items quickly and want to point at a row instead of counting keystrokes.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to click or tap a row in the work item list so the selection moves to that item.
- As a Herdr user, I want to double-click or double-tap an item so it opens in the detail view (same as pressing Enter).
- As a Herdr user, I want to scroll the mouse wheel (or a two-finger touch scroll) in the list so the selection moves up/down like the arrow keys.
- As a Herdr user, I want to scroll the wheel in the detail view so the description scrolls without using keys.
- As a Herdr user, I want to tap a stage option in the filter prompt so the filter is applied without typing digits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mouse tracking is enabled/disabled with the TUI lifecycle**: entering raw mode emits the mouse-tracking enable sequences (`\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1002h\x1b[?1006h` — button-event tracking + SGR extended coordinates); cleanup/exit emits the matching disable sequences. Verified by test (sequence strings are emitted on setup/cleanup) and manual smoke-run.
2. **Click/tap selects a row**: a single left click/tap on a visible list row moves the selection to that item (equivalent of the up/down arrow keys). Verified by unit tests on the row-mapping + dispatch logic.
3. **Double-click/tap opens details**: two clicks within the double-click window on the same row activate that item (equivalent of Enter), including from the detail view back to the list. Verified by unit test.
4. **Wheel and touch-scroll navigate**: wheel-up/wheel-down (buttons 64/65) and equivalent touch scrolls move the selection in list mode and scroll the detail content in detail mode (page/line scroll consistent with keyboard `j`/`k`). Verified by unit test.
5. **Filter prompt is pointer-sensitive**: tapping a stage option row in the filter prompt applies that stage filter (equivalent of pressing the digit key). Verified by unit test.
6. **Keyboard navigation is unaffected**: all existing key sequences still behave as before; unparsable/unknown mouse sequences are ignored without crashing or corrupting state. Existing `handleKeypress` tests continue to pass.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries (e.g., docs/dev/ input-handling notes).
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Mouse support is **additive** — existing keyboard navigation (arrows, `j`/`k`, Enter, Escape, chords) must keep working unchanged.
- Must work through the terminal's standard mouse-reporting protocol: SGR mouse events (`\x1b[<b;x;yM` press / `\x1b[<b;x;y m` release), with coordinates 1-based. Touch events arrive translated as mouse events (tap = left click, drag = motion, two-finger scroll = wheel) in terminals that support it — the plugin must not require any terminal-specific feature beyond SGR reporting (widely supported: xterm, tmux, kitty, wezterm, iTerm2, Windows Terminal).
- Drag-motion events (button code with the 32 motion bit) must not cause accidental selection jumps; motion is either used for an explicit touch-drag scroll or ignored safely.
- Mouse sequences arrive as raw stdin chunks (e.g. `\x1b[<0;10;5M`); they must be detected and consumed before the existing keypress parser sees them, and must not be mistaken for arrow-key escape sequences.
- The pane-hidden pause logic (pause-when-hidden) is out of scope — input is not read while the pane is hidden anyway.
- Fallback: terminals without mouse reporting simply never send mouse events; the list remains fully keyboard-usable (fail-soft).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (2790 lines) is the selection-list TUI: `runWorklistTui` sets raw mode (`process.stdin.setRawMode(true)`), reads input via `process.stdin.on('data', onData)`, and dispatches through `handleKeypress(state, key, termSize)` → `keyToAction(key)`.
- No mouse-tracking escape sequences are emitted; no SGR mouse events are parsed. Unknown sequences currently fall through `keyToAction` to `default → null`.
- `ANSI` constants object (line 132) already holds terminal escapes — the natural home for mouse enable/disable sequences.
- Rendering computes row geometry in `createListRenderer`: a header row at the top, the list area (`listArea = rows - 1 - panelHeight`), a notification row, and a metadata panel at the bottom. Detail mode renders a `formatDetailView` block; filter mode renders `formatFilterPrompt` with digit-key stage options.
- Tests live in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (vitest); `handleKeypress` is a pure function tested directly — the new mouse logic should follow the same pattern (pure, unit-testable).

## Desired change

1. Add ANSI constants for mouse tracking enable (`\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1002h\x1b[?1006h`) and disable (`\x1b[?1000l\x1b[?1002l\x1b[?1006l`).
2. In `runWorklistTui`, emit enable sequences when entering raw mode and disable sequences in `cleanup()`.
3. Add a pure `parseMouseEvent(key: string)` helper that recognizes `\x1b[<...M`/`\x1b[<...m` and returns `{ button, x, y, release } | null`.
4. Add a pure row-mapping helper that converts a click's 1-based `y` into a list row (accounting for the header offset and `scrollOffset`), a detail-view scroll position, or a filter-prompt option, depending on `state.mode`.
5. Add `mapMouseToAction(state, mouseEvent, termSize)` returning an action (`select-row`, `open-detail`, `wheel-up/down`, `scroll-detail`, `filter-stage`, etc.) and dispatch it from `onData` before the keypress path; track last-click time/position for double-click detection (~400 ms window).
6. Add unit tests mirroring the existing `handleKeypress` suite: parser, row mapping per mode, wheel dispatch, double-click window, filter-tap, and "unknown mouse sequence is ignored" regression.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — mouse enable/disable sequences, SGR event parser, row→item mapping, mouse dispatch in `onData`, double-click detection (primary change).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — unit tests for the parser, per-mode mapping, wheel/double-click/filter-tap dispatch, and unknown-sequence regression.
- `packages/herdr/dist/` — rebuilt artifacts via `npm run build` (tsc), kept in sync with source.
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — documents the input/refresh loop; add a note about mouse input if behavior interacts with it (minor).

## Related work

- `Create a work item selection list in Herdr (WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP)` — the parent feature that built this list; its AC #5 defined keyboard navigation, this item extends input to pointers.
- `Impl: visibility-gated auto-refresh/sync in worklist TUI (WL-0MSB4473J004NYO5)` — owns the input loop/timers this change touches (input is only read while the pane is visible).
- `Mouse click on Work Items tree does not update details (WL-0MLAJ3Z750G25EJE)` — historical pointer bug in the older Pi TUI; the click-select behavior contract should match (click selects, details follow).
- `Critical: TUI closes when clicking anywhere (WL-0MKX2C2X007IRR8G)` — historical mouse-handling crash; regression tests here must prove unknown mouse sequences are inert.
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — architecture notes for the worklist input/refresh loop.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** Herdr's terminal supports SGR mouse reporting (1006) — all mainstream terminals do; if not, events simply never arrive (fail-soft, keyboard remains fully usable).
- **Risk — mouse sequences misparsed as keys:** raw chunks like `\x1b[<0;10;5M` must be fully consumed by the mouse path; partial-buffer splits (a chunk split across reads) must be buffered until the terminating `M`/`m`. Mitigated by dedicated parser tests including split-chunk cases.
- **Risk — drag-motion events:** button codes with the 32 motion bit arrive during drags; guard so motion never jumps the selection. Out of scope: implementing drag-to-scroll as a scroll gesture (recorded as a follow-up opportunity rather than expanding scope).
- **Risk — double-click timing:** a ~400 ms window is standard; on slow terminals two intentional clicks may land outside it — acceptable, Enter remains available.
- **Risk — regression to chord/agent shortcuts:** mouse input must not intercept or swallow chord leader keys; the keypress path is unchanged except that mouse-shaped sequences are consumed first.
- **Scope-creep guard:** hover highlighting, drag-to-scroll, right-click context menus, and horizontal touch gestures are NOT in scope; if valuable, they should be captured as linked work items, not added to this item.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU** – Add links to dependencies in the metadata output of the details pane in the TUI. (open)
- **WL-0MSGAEXER000707R** – Pi agent pane opened via a+a (audit) starts in herdr plugin source dir, not the project root (completed)
- **WL-0MNC79G3P004NZXH** – Markdown formatting in Description and Comments field (completed)

- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/skill/intakeall/tests/test_intakeall.py` — matched: events, item, list, make, packages, sensitive, support, touch, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/command/intake.md` — matched: events, intent, item, list, seed, sensitive, support, work

---

## Plan (generated 2026-08-07 by /skill:plan)

**Approach:** Additive mouse/touch support over the existing SGR mouse-reporting protocol, behind the existing raw-mode lifecycle, with a pure-function parser/dispatch design mirroring `handleKeypress` (unit-testable, fail-soft). Decomposed into 4 vertical slices (test-first) + 1 recorded follow-up.

### Features (child work items)

1. **Test: mouse input handling suite** (WL-0MSI720DX002E9WC) — `task`, high. Test-first suite covering all 8 parent ACs: lifecycle sequence emission, SGR parser incl. split chunks, per-mode row mapping, click/double-click/wheel/filter-tap dispatch, drag-motion guard, unknown-sequence inertness, keyboard regression.
2. **Implement: mouse tracking lifecycle + SGR parser** (WL-0MSI7278X0008XGM) — `feature`, medium. ANSI enable/disable constants, emit on raw-mode entry / cleanup, pure `parseMouseEvent` with chunk buffering. Depends on 1.
3. **Implement: mouse dispatch and interactions** (WL-0MSI72EYW00050N2) — `feature`, medium. Row mapping per mode, `mapMouseToAction`, dispatch from `onData` before keypress path, ~400 ms double-click window, wheel/touch scroll (list selection + detail scroll incl. ToC-focus nuance), filter-prompt tap, drag-motion guard. Depends on 1, 2.
4. **Docs, build and verification** (WL-0MSI72L3O005BIW5) — `task`, medium. Update `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` + README notes, rebuild `packages/herdr/dist`, full suite green, manual smoke-run evidence comment. Depends on 3.

- **Follow-up: drag-to-scroll in Herdr worklist** (WL-0MSI72S0Y0060BRK) — `feature`, low, sibling with `discovered-from:WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ`. Drag/touch-drag scroll; must respect the drag-motion guard.

# Show plugin version in Herdr work item selection list (WL-0MSGKEBFU004T3N3)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Worklog work item selection list gives no indication of which plugin version is running, making it hard to verify installs, spot stale builds, or report bugs accurately. A dimmed, right-aligned version number in the pane header solves this without visual clutter.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who want to confirm which version of the Worklog Selection List plugin is running.
- **Developers/support** who need the version handy when filing bug reports or verifying an updated build is live.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the plugin version in the corner of the work item list, so I can confirm which build I'm running.
- As a developer, I want the version visible but unobtrusive, so it doesn't distract from the list content.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Problem statement

In the herdr work item selection list, the metadata panel for the selected item shows the work item ID twice: once in the panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) and again as the first row of the metadata data table (`ID  WL-XXXX`). The ID row in the data table is redundant and should be dropped, leaving the ID only in the panel title line.

## Users

Users navigating work items in the herdr selection list (`prefix+l`).

**User story:** As a user browsing work items in the herdr selection list, I want the item ID shown once in the metadata panel so the panel is not redundant and the layout is cleaner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The metadata data table in the herdr metadata panel no longer contains an `ID` row.
- [ ] The metadata panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) still shows the item ID.
- [ ] Other metadata rows (Status, Stage, Priority, Title, etc.) render unchanged.
- [ ] The detail view (`formatDetailContent`) behavior is unchanged (it already omits ID/Title from its table since they appear in its header).
- [ ] Tests are added/updated covering the metadata panel output (e.g. the `formatMetadataPanel` describe block in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix should follow the existing pattern used by the detail view (`formatDetailContent` filters `ID`/`Title` out of the table since they are in the header).
- No behavior change to the CLI `show` output or other renderers.

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:

- `formatMetadataPanel` (line ~874) renders the panel header separator `── ${item.id} ──` (line ~891) and then the metadata table from `buildMetaRows(item)` (line ~894).
- `buildMetaRows` (line ~828) unconditionally adds the ID as the first row via `addMeta('ID', item.id)` (line ~835).
- The detail view `formatDetailContent` (line ~969) already filters `ID` and `Title` out of the shared table because both appear in its header: `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID' && label !== 'Title')`.

So the metadata panel currently shows the ID in both the header line and the first data row — the inconsistency with the detail view.

## Desired change

Remove the `ID` row from the metadata table rendered in the metadata panel, consistent with how `formatDetailContent` handles it. The header line `── WL-XXXX ──` continues to display the ID. The `Title` row should remain in the metadata panel table since the panel header does not show the title.

Likely approach: in `formatMetadataPanel`, filter the `ID` row from `buildMetaRows(item)` output (e.g. `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID')`), mirroring `formatDetailContent`. Alternatively, remove `addMeta('ID', item.id)` from `buildMetaRows` — but note `formatDetailContent` relies on `buildMetaRows` including ID then filtering it, so removing it from the shared builder is also safe as long as tests are updated. Prefer the filter-in-panel approach for minimal blast radius.

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel — field rendering and scrolling` describe block (~line 896); add a test asserting the data table no longer contains an `ID` row while the header still shows the ID. # Detail view ToC overflows pane — first lines scroll off the top of the screen

## Problem statement

In the Herdr plugin's work-item detail view, when an item has a `Related Docs` Table of Contents (ToC) (i.e. ≥1 `.md` Key File), the rendered output exceeds the pane height: the header (id/title) and the first ToC lines scroll off the top of the screen, so the ToC is not entirely visible. The ToC is also rendered twice and the item header is dropped entirely.

## Users

- **Herdr users** viewing a work item's detail view in the plugin pane, who need the item header and the full `Related Docs` ToC visible at the top of the pane while the metadata/description/document body scrolls beneath.

### Example User Stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the item id, title, and the complete Related Docs ToC when I open a work item's detail view, so nothing important is cut off at the top of the screen.
- As a Herdr user, I want the ToC to stay pinned while I scroll the document, so I can always see which documents are linked to the item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an item has a ToC (≥1 `.md` Key File), the detail view shows the header (id, title, separator) and the **full** ToC at the top of the pane at scroll 0 — no lines cut off. The ToC is rendered **exactly once** (no duplication), and the item header is present.
2. Detail-view output never exceeds the pane: `formatDetailView` returns at most `viewportHeight` lines, and the full renderer (`createListRenderer` detail mode) returns at most `rows - 1` lines — the line-count invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO holds for detail mode with a ToC present.
3. The header + ToC block stays **pinned** at the top while the body (metadata table, description, md viewer) scrolls beneath it; scrolling is limited to the body region (viewport height minus the pinned block height), and `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` clamps against the same reduced body viewport. No dead/blank region at the bottom when fully scrolled.
4. Items **without** `.md` Key Files (no ToC) keep the existing full-scroll behavior unchanged (regression check — no behavior change for the no-ToC path).
5. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: line-count invariant for detail mode with ToC (renderer ≤ `rows - 1`; `formatDetailView` ≤ `viewportHeight`), header + ToC fully visible at scroll 0, ToC not duplicated, pinned-ToC scroll regression (existing `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'` test kept green/updated), and no-ToC behavior unchanged.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant README/docs entries describing the detail-view ToC layout (`packages/herdr/README.md`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Preserve the pinned-ToC design from WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I / WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29: the ToC stays visible on all renders; only the body below it scrolls.
- Respect the line-count invariant established in WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO: the renderer must never emit more than `rows - 1` lines, otherwise the terminal scrolls the top of the output off the pane.
- Surgical change: do not alter scrolling behavior for items without a ToC (the pre-existing full-scroll path).
- No new dependencies; reuse the existing `formatDetailToC` / `formatDetailContent` helpers.

## Existing state

- `formatDetailView` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, ~line 1223) builds the detail output as `[...tocLines, ...bodyLines.slice(safeOffset, safeOffset + viewportHeight)]` where `bodyLines = allLines.slice(tocLines.length)`.
- The slicing assumes the ToC occupies the first `tocLines.length` lines of `allLines`, but `formatDetailContent` emits the header first (blank, id, title, separator = 4 lines) and the ToC **after** it. Consequences (verified by reproduction): (a) the header is dropped from the output, (b) the ToC is duplicated (once from `tocLines`, once inside `bodyLines`), (c) total output = `viewportHeight + tocLines.length` lines, which overflows the pane (`viewportHeight = rows - 1` in the renderer). Reproduction: `formatDetailView(item, 80, 0, 20)` with a 2-entry ToC returns 26 lines; the renderer on a 24-row terminal emits 29 lines (max allowed 23).
- Regression introduced in commit `76a52c9f` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I, "Implementation complete").
- `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` (~line 496) computes `maxScroll` against the full `viewportHeight` instead of the body region, so clamping is also wrong for the pinned layout.
- The existing test `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'` only asserts the ToC appears in the first 8 lines — it never checks the total line count, so it passes despite the overflow.

## Desired change

1. In `formatDetailView`, compute a **pinned block** = header (4 lines: blank, id, title, separator) + `tocLines`; the scrollable **body** = `allLines.slice(pinnedHeight)`; the **body viewport** = `max(1, viewportHeight - pinnedHeight)`; `maxScroll = max(0, bodyLines.length - bodyViewport)`. Render `[...pinned, ...bodyLines.slice(safeOffset, safeOffset + bodyViewport)]` and update the scroll-indicator percentage math to use `bodyViewport`.
2. Keep the no-ToC path (`tocLines.length === 0`) identical to the pre-ToC behavior (whole content scrolls, header included) to avoid scope creep.
3. Update `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` to clamp against the reduced body viewport (subtract the pinned height) so `j`/`G` behave consistently with the renderer.
4. Optionally introduce a named constant (e.g. `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES = 4`) documenting the fixed header shape so the slicing is self-explanatory.
5. Add/extend unit tests per AC5; update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it describes the detail-view layout.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatDetailView` pinned header+ToC slicing and body-viewport math; `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` clamp; optional header-lines constant.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — line-count invariant tests for detail mode with ToC, header/ToC visibility at scroll 0, no-duplication check, no-ToC regression, updated pinned-ToC test.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the pinned header + ToC detail-view layout if it describes the ToC behavior.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Header-shape fragility:** the fix relies on the header being exactly 4 lines (blank, id, title, separator). Mitigate by introducing a named `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES` constant next to `formatDetailContent` and by an AC1 test asserting the header is visible at scroll 0.
- **No-ToC regression:** altering `formatDetailView` slicing could accidentally change the full-scroll path for items without `.md` Key Files. Mitigate with AC4 regression test asserting the no-ToC path is unchanged.
- **Viewport-height mismatch:** the state class uses `rows - 4` while the renderer uses `rows - 1`; today the renderer's clamp absorbs the difference. The fix must subtract the pinned height consistently in both `formatDetailView` and `detailScrollDown` so `j`/`G` and the on-screen clamp agree.
- **Scope creep:** pinning the header for ALL items (even without a ToC) is deliberately out of scope — it is a UX change beyond the reported bug. Recorded as an assumption; can be tracked as a separate work item if desired.
- **Assumption:** the fix pins header + ToC together (the header sits above the ToC in the content stream, so pinning the ToC keeps the header visible) and scrolls only the body (metadata/description/md viewer) beneath — faithful to the pinned-ToC design intent (WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 AC3) and the user's expectation that the first lines be visible.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I` (completed) — "Herdr: detail-view ToC for Related Docs (arrow/j/k navigate, Enter renders)" — the pinned-ToC implementation that introduced this regression (commit `76a52c9f`).
- `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` (completed) — "Herdr plugin: add Related Docs row to metadata section listing .md Key Files (openable in the markdown viewer)" — defines the pinned-ToC design intent.
- `WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO` (completed) — "Herdr: pane line-count invariant (rows - 1)" — the invariant the detail view now violates.
- `WL-0MS31WX9C008FIQR` (completed) — "Full scrollable detail view" — original detail-view scrolling design (whole content scrolls).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required for this intake.

- The seed report ("The table of contents on the detail view of work items is not entirely visible — the first few lines are off the top of the screen") combined with repository analysis was conclusive: the root cause was located by inspection of `formatDetailView`/`formatDetailContent` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, confirmed by a reproduction test (26 lines emitted for a 20-line viewport; 29 lines for a 24-row terminal vs. the 23-line invariant), and pinned to the regression commit `76a52c9f` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I) via `git log -S`.
- Assumption (documented, user can override): the fix pins the **header + ToC** block at the top of the detail view (the header is above the ToC in the content stream, so pinning the ToC necessarily keeps the header visible) while the body scrolls beneath — this is the faithful reading of the pinned-ToC design intent in WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 AC3 ("The ToC stays visible on all renders") and the user's expectation that the first lines be visible.
- Assumption (documented, user can override): items **without** `.md` Key Files keep the existing full-scroll behavior unchanged (surgical scope).

---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKXJPCDI1FLYDB1** – Prompt input box must resize on word wrap (completed)
- **WL-0MRMCO4WX0073W30** – Arbitrary-depth chords in detail view (completed)
- **WL-0MQQW534Q009JSX7** – Remove superfluous ## Stage section from wl create output (completed)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: detail, entirely, first, items, lines (+11 more)

## Summary

Ensure the herdr audit-freshness predicate enforces the canonical "at-or-near"
semantics and is the **single source of truth** shared by both the icon display
and the downtime (audit-dispatch) worker.

Audit freshness currently lives only in `isAuditFresh()` in
`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`. It is the basis for the icon display
(`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) AND is the documented freshness gate reused by the
downtime dispatch audit tier (`selectAuditCandidate` /
`getNextAuditCandidate` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, which
treats `!isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` as "needs a fresh `/skill:audit`").

Running an audit itself bumps the work item's `updatedAt` to within a fraction
of a second of its `auditedAt` (`wl audit-set` + `wl update --audit-text` +
the verdict-driven status transition). A freshness rule that requires a strict
gap on one side (e.g. only `auditedAt` comfortably ahead of `updatedAt`) can
therefore disagree with the just-persisted state. The canonical fix in
SorraAgents (SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4) treats an audit as fresh when its
`auditedAt` is **at or near** the item's `updatedAt` (within a small
tolerance) because a near-simultaneous `updatedAt` bump is the audit's own
persistence write.

This item makes ContextHub's herdr audit-freshness logic follow the same
at-or-near rule so the icon display and the downtime dispatcher agree, and
never disagree on a just-persisted audit.

## Expected behaviour

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` returns true (fresh) when `auditedAt`
  is at-or-near `updatedAt` within a small, named tolerance (the audit's own
  persistence write), and false otherwise.
- The icon (`auditIcon` in `icons.ts`) shows the fresh icon for a
  just-persisted audit (no longer shows the stale glyph for an audit the run
  just persisted).
- The downtime audit candidate selection (`selectAuditCandidate` /
  `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`) uses the SAME
  `isAuditFresh` predicate, so a just-persisted fresh audit is NOT a dispatch
  candidate (no redundant `/skill:audit` re-run).
- Only one freshness definition exists; neither consumer re-implements its
  own comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditFresh` in `icons.ts` treats `auditedAt` at-or-near `updatedAt`
   (within a documented tolerance constant) as fresh, covering the
   audit-persistence case (`auditedAt ~ updatedAt`, delta well under the
   tolerance).
2. A unit test asserts `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` is true for a
   just-persisted audit (auditedAt and updatedAt differ by milliseconds).
3. A unit test asserts a genuinely stale audit (item updated well after the
   audit) is still false (stale), unchanged.
4. `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate` in `downtime-worker.ts`
   continue to use the imported `isAuditFresh` as the sole filter; a
   just-persisted fresh item is excluded from candidates.
5. Both consumers import the same helper; no competing freshness comparison
   is introduced in the dispatch or icon paths.

## Notes / Open questions

- `isAuditFresh` currently hard-codes a magic `60000` ms literal. Prefer
  naming a constant (e.g. `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS`) and routing
  both consumers through it.
- Reconcile the comparison shape of `isAuditFresh` (`auditTime > updateTime -
  buffer`) with the canonical at-or-near semantics from the SorraAgents fix so
  both projects express the same intent. Confirm the target semantics with the
  operator before implementing.

## References

- discovered-from: SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4 (SorraAgents audit_runner child
  freshness at-or-near fix) — canonical reference implementation.
- related-to: WL-0MSI9FK2Q0074C31 (Audit candidate selection),
  WL-0MSI9WPNI0044R (Audit dispatch tier), parent WL-0MSI8H3HP700K0RG.

## Problem statement

SorraAgents is the canonical installer for pi agent guidance: its scripts/install_pi.sh symlinks the global guidance (AGENTS_GLOBAL.md -> ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md, plus skills and prompts) into every project. The global AGENTS.md already contains the full agent workflow (work-item lifecycle, implement/build-test-commit order, push policy, triage policy).

ContextHub's 'wl init' (src/commands/init.ts) currently has overlapping responsibilities: it prompts for a workflow choice (promptWorkflowChoice: N / B / M, where M is 'Manage custom workflow by editing AGENTS.md directly') and, via ensureWorkflowTemplateInstalled / insertWorkflowLoaderIntoAgents, can inline WORKFLOW content into the project's AGENTS.md. When the SorraAgents global install is present this creates two sources of truth for agent workflow guidance and can conflict with the canonical global file.

## User story

# Herdr selection list: gate background/foreground sync on DB-update check before spawning wl commands

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list spawns a burst of `wl` CLI processes on a fixed cadence — background `wl sync` every 60s plus a full refresh (`wl next`, 2× `wl list` mandatory subsets, expanded-children fetches) on every 30s auto-refresh tick — **regardless of whether the worklog database changed**. When the pane is idle (no agents writing, no remote activity), each cycle wastes 3–5 process spawns and a full git sync round-trip for zero visible change.

## Users

- **Herdr users running the selection list with auto-refresh/auto-sync on** — want the list to stay current without constant background `wl` process churn (spawn overhead, git fetch/pull/merge/push, lock contention with other panes).
- **Multi-pane / multi-agent setups** — the reduction in unnecessary `wl sync` invocations reduces lock-storm pressure between panes and cross-process DB churn.

Example user stories:
- As a Herdr user with an idle backlog, I want the selection list to avoid spawning any `wl` commands when nothing changed, so my machine isn't churning processes and git round-trips every 30–60s.
- As a Herdr user, I want background sync to still run at least once per configurable window (default 60s) even when nothing changed locally, so I still receive remote changes pushed by other machines.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On an auto-refresh tick, when the worklog DB has not changed since the last refresh cycle, the pane spawns **zero** `wl` processes for that tick (no `wl next`, no `wl list`, no children fetches, no `wl sync`, no action-count fetch).
2. On an auto-sync tick, `wl sync` is skipped when (a) the DB has not changed since the last cycle **and** (b) the last successful sync is fresher than the configurable max-staleness cap (default 60s). If either condition fails, the sync runs (subject to the existing heartbeat / single-flight / `--if-idle` guards).
3. The max-staleness cap is configurable via the Herdr settings file (e.g. new `maxSyncStalenessMs` setting, default `60000`), clamped to a sane minimum like the sync interval clamp.
4. Manual user actions — `S` (sync) and `r` (refresh) keypresses — always run, ignoring the gate.
5. The very first cycle after pane start always runs (no prior "last seen" signal), and any failure to read the DB-change signal fails **open** (the cycle runs), so the list can never go stale due to a signal-read error.
6. The existing cross-instance heartbeat (`last-sync-time`), single-flight, and `--if-idle` guards remain in place for syncs that do run.
7. Unit tests cover: gate skip/run decisions for refresh and sync ticks (changed/unchanged DB, stale/fresh last-sync, manual override, first-cycle, fail-open), plus the new setting's parse/clamp behavior.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin package (`packages/herdr`) has **zero npm dependencies** and intentionally duplicates small shared helpers per TUI (decision Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B) — a small pure helper duplicating the counter-read logic is consistent with this pattern.
- The DB-change signal must be cheap (a file read or two) and must NOT spawn a `wl` process itself — that is the whole point of the gate.
- The signal must be cross-process stable: the wl CLI read cache (F2) deliberately avoids SQLite file mtimes because "the SQLite files are rewritten by the app on every open/close cycle… file-based fingerprints are not stable across processes" (`src/read-cache.ts`). The gate must not produce false "changed" signals from the pane's own reads.
- Do not change wl CLI sync behavior itself; the incremental-sync work (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q) is separate scope.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `runWorklistTui` registers two scheduler tasks: `refresh` (every `refreshIntervalMs`, default 30s, always calls `doRefresh(false)` → spawns read commands) and `sync` (every `syncIntervalMs`, default 60s, calls `doSync(true, heartbeatTtlMs)` then `doRefresh(false)`). Plus a `resume-poll` task that calls `doRefresh(true)` on hidden→visible transition.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — `runSync` spawns `wl sync` fire-and-forget with cross-instance heartbeat skip (`last-sync-time` marker, `isSyncHeartbeatFresh`), single-flight guard, and `--if-idle`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — all read commands (`wl next`, `wl list`, children, action-count) go through `runWl`; the CLI serves many from its on-disk read cache (F2), but a process spawn still occurs per command.
- `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — the wl CLI maintains a monotonic per-worklog-dir **state counter** (`~/.cache/wl/state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json`, `{ "state": N }`), bumped by every wl write command and by post-sync invalidation (`invalidateCacheForWrite`). This is the natural "DB changed" signal: cross-process, stable across reads, and already the CLI's freshness authority.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — typed settings JSON with clamped intervals; `syncIntervalMs` has a 60s minimum clamp.
- Manual `S`/`r` keypresses dispatch to `doSync()` / `doRefresh(true)` unconditionally.

## Desired change

- Add a small pure module in `packages/herdr` (e.g. `db-change.ts`) that:
  - resolves the wl cache dir (mirroring `resolveCacheDir()` precedence: `WL_CACHE_DIR` → `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/wl` → `~/.cache/wl`);
  - reads the state counter for the resolved worklog dir (`state/<sha256(worklogDir)>.json`), returning the counter value (0 when absent); and
  - exposes a `DbChangeTracker`/helper that remembers the last-seen counter per pane and answers `dbChangedSinceLastCycle()` (fail-open: any read error ⇒ true).
- Gate the scheduler tasks in `runWorklistTui`:
  - `refresh` tick: skip (spawn nothing) when the DB is unchanged since the last cycle.
  - `sync` tick: skip `wl sync` when DB unchanged **and** last successful sync (heartbeat marker) is within the configurable max-staleness cap; otherwise run `doSync` + `doRefresh` as today.
  - `resume-poll` hidden→visible transition: apply the same DB-change gate (list content is identical when nothing changed).
  - Manual `S`/`r` paths unchanged (always run).
- Add the configurable cap to settings (e.g. `maxSyncStalenessMs`, default 60s, clamped ≥1s or aligned with the sync-interval clamp) and pass it through `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`.
- Keep all existing guards (heartbeat, single-flight, `--if-idle`) for syncs that do run.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts` — NEW: pure DB-change signal reader (wl cache-dir resolution + state-counter read + last-seen tracker), fail-open.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — expose/adapt staleness helpers (reuse `readSyncHeartbeatMs`) so the sync tick can decide "DB unchanged AND sync fresh ⇒ skip".
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — wire the gate into the `refresh` / `sync` / `resume-poll` scheduler tasks; manual `S`/`r` untouched.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — new `maxSyncStalenessMs` setting (default `60000`) with clamping.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the new setting into `runWorklistTui`.
- `src/read-cache.ts` — read-only reference for the counter-file format/path derivation (no changes expected).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/db-change.test.ts` (NEW), plus updates to `auto-sync.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts`.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W` — Cross-instance sync heartbeat (F3): the `last-sync-time` marker and heartbeat TTL this change composes with. Completed.
- `WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E` — wl sync lock storm: auto-sync single-flight / `--if-idle` guards; gating reduces spawn pressure further. Completed.
- `WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA` — wl CLI read cache (F2) with the state-counter fingerprint this gate reuses as its signal. Completed.
- `WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q` — Incremental sync: only export/push changed work items (CLI-side; explicitly out of scope here). Open.
- `WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B` — Smart-selection duplication decision (Q2c): precedent for duplicating a small pure helper into the Herdr package. Completed.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — release workflow (no code impact; doc reference).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Remote-pull latency (accepted tradeoff, user-confirmed):** skipping `wl sync` when the DB is unchanged delays pulling remote changes until the next sync that does run. Bounded by the max-staleness cap (default 60s) so remote freshness is never worse than the cap.
- **Signal completeness:** the state counter is bumped by wl CLI writes and post-sync invalidation. External tools writing the SQLite DB directly (not via wl) would not bump it — mitigated by the staleness cap, which forces a periodic sync regardless. Assumed acceptable.
- **Configurable cap naming/units:** `maxSyncStalenessMs` in ms, default 60000, clamped to ≥1s (aligned with `heartbeatTtlForInterval`'s clamp) — exact name subject to implementer/plan review.
- **Scope-creep guard:** incremental sync (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q), event-driven window subscription (WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ), and WAL checkpointing (WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I) are tracked separately and must NOT be pulled into this work item.
- **Behavioral parity:** when the DB IS changing, cadence must match today (no additional latency); only the no-change case adds skipping.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (asked 2026-08-07): "If the local DB hasn't changed, should the background `wl sync` also be skipped? That means remote changes pushed by other machines would only be pulled when local activity bumps the counter (or via manual `S`). Acceptable — or should the sync path stay ungated while only the refresh reads are skipped?" — Answer (user): "Partially acceptable. wl sync can be skipped if no local DB changes. However, it should not go more than 1 minute (configurable) without being run." Source: interactive reply. → Implemented as AC2/AC3: sync is gated by (DB unchanged AND last successful sync within configurable max-staleness cap, default 60s).
- Q2 (asked 2026-08-07): "Should manual refresh (`r`) and manual sync (`S`) always run regardless of the check? (My assumption: yes — user-initiated actions always execute.)" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply. → Implemented as AC4.
- Q3 (asked 2026-08-07, /skill:find-related): "Which work items are related?" — Research: the find-related script (`find_related.py --work-item-id WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ`) resolved the wrong worklog store (SorraAgents framework repo) on both runs and returned unrelated items (OpenBrain submission, file-path convention, a-y shortcut). The matches were excluded per the skill's conservative policy (false negatives preferred); the curated Related work section above (verified via `wl show` against the ContextHub store) is authoritative.

# Intake Brief: Colour code work items by priority in selection lists (CLI + Herdr)

**Work Item ID:** WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6

**Headline:** Colour coding of work items in the selection list should be based on **priority**, not stage: critical are red, low are dimmed, medium is white, high is orange — recorded in a shared theme file.

## Problem Statement

Work item titles in selection lists are currently coloured by **stage** (progression: gray → blue → cyan → yellow → green → white, from WL-0MQ53H78W000DQ08). Stage progression communicates workflow position, but operators scanning a list need to see **priority** at a glance — critical items should jump out in red, low-priority items should recede. The colour scheme must be defined once in a shared theme file.

## Users

All Worklog users viewing work item lists:

- **Operators and agents** scanning `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent` need immediate visual cue of what matters (critical = red, high = orange).
- **Herdr users** browsing the Worklog selection list pane need the same priority cue.

Example user stories:
- "As an operator, I want critical work items to appear red so I can immediately spot what needs attention."
- "As an agent, I want low-priority items dimmed so they recede while scanning the list."
- "As a project manager, I want a consistent priority colour scheme across the CLI and the Herdr selection list, defined in one shared theme file."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The canonical priority colour mapping is recorded in the shared theme file `src/theme.ts`:
   - `critical` → red
   - `high` → orange
   - `medium` → white
   - `low` → dimmed
2. Work item **titles** are coloured by priority and work item **ids** are coloured by stage, everywhere they appear: `wl list`, `wl search`, `wl recent`, `wl show`, `wl next`, and the Herdr worklist selection list (`formatItemLine`).
3. Blocked items no longer receive the unconditional red override; they are coloured by their natural priority like every other item (per clarification Q3b).
4. Unknown/missing priority falls back to a sensible default colour (e.g. medium/white) and unknown/missing stage keeps a sensible default (gray) — matching current fallback behaviour.
5. Unit tests cover the new priority colour mapping and the title/priority + id/stage split in both the CLI helpers (`src/commands/helpers.ts`) and the Herdr icons (`packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`), including blocked and unknown-priority cases.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr/`) is a separate package depending only on `@worklog/shared`; it renders raw ANSI 256-colour escape codes and cannot import `src/theme.ts` (which depends on chalk).
- The Pi-based TUI extension (`packages/tui/`) is **out of scope** — it is slated for removal (see WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N) and colours via Pi theme tokens, not the theme file.
- "Orange" should use a colour consistent with the existing `theme.text.readyNo` (`chalk.hex('#FFA500')`).
- No new dependencies.

## Existing state

- `src/theme.ts` already has a `priority` map (`critical: chalk.redBright`, `high: chalk.yellowBright`, `medium: chalk.blueBright`, `low: chalk.gray`), a `stage` progression map, and a `blocked: chalk.redBright` override.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `renderTitle()` colours the title by stage (`titleColorForStage`), with a blocked override checked first; `formatTitleAndId()` renders the id muted (`theme.text.muted`); `humanFormatWorkItem()` also renders ids muted in several formats.
- Herdr: `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` has `stageColor()` / `applyStageColour()`; `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `formatItemLine()` colours the title by stage and leaves the id uncoloured. `STAGE_COLORS` (worklist.ts) is reused by the stage-filter dialog and separators.

## Desired change

- **`src/theme.ts`:** update `priority` colours to red / orange / white / dim. Keep the `stage` map (now used for ids). Remove the `blocked` override (per Q3b) or leave it unused — implementer decision, but `renderTitle` must no longer apply it.
- **`src/commands/helpers.ts`:** `renderTitle()` colours by priority (fallback for unknown priority); `formatTitleAndId()` and `humanFormatWorkItem()` colour ids by stage instead of muted. This automatically covers list, search, recent, show, next.
- **Herdr `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`:** add `priorityColor(priority)` / `applyPriorityColour(text, priority)` using ANSI 256 codes (red ≈ 196, orange ≈ 208, white ≈ 15, dim ≈ 241). Keep `stageColor` / `applyStageColour` for ids.
- **Herdr `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:** `formatItemLine()` — title via priority colour, id via stage colour. Keep `STAGE_COLORS` for the stage filter dialog and separators.
- **Shared theme consideration:** the priority colour *spec* lives in `src/theme.ts`. To prevent drift between the CLI (chalk) and Herdr (ANSI), consider extracting a colour-name spec (e.g. a `packages/shared` module mapping priority → colour name, consumed by both) — at minimum the two maps must stay consistent. Flag as design decision for the implementer; do not over-engineer.

## Key Files:

- `src/theme.ts` — canonical priority colour mapping (red/orange/white/dim); stage map retained for ids
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `renderTitle` (priority colour), `formatTitleAndId` / `humanFormatWorkItem` (stage-coloured ids)
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — add `priorityColor` / `applyPriorityColour` (ANSI 256)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatItemLine` title/priority + id/stage split

## Related work

- **WL-0MQ53H78W000DQ08** (completed, high) — "Refactor colour mappings: remove status-based colours, use stage progression with blocked override". Established the current stage-based scheme this item replaces for titles. See `src/theme.ts`, `src/commands/helpers.ts`.
- **WL-0MQ8LKXH20058N1M** (completed, high) — "Consistent colour scheme for work item titles in Blessed and Pi TUIs". Earlier consistency work; Pi TUI out of scope here.
- **WL-0MP15YIQ200748RC / WL-0MP15YJ4A0031YGR** (completed) — "Implement colour mapping in TUI and CLI" and its test item.
- **WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N** (open, high) — "Remove the Pi-based TUI from the repo; keep the agent-side Pi plugin features" — Pi TUI excluded from this scope.
- **WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY** (open, high) — "Herdr selection list: sort by priority first, then stage" — sibling priority-related change to the same Herdr worklist.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Selection list" = `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent` / `wl show` outputs plus the Herdr worklist pane (confirmed by user: "both a and b plus the herdr plugin").
- **Assumption:** Title = priority colour, id = stage colour, everywhere (confirmed: "Always use priority in title and stage colouring in id (everywhere they appear)").
- **Assumption:** Blocked items show their natural priority colour; the always-red blocked override is removed (confirmed: Q3 answer "b").
- **Risk:** CLI and Herdr colour maps drifting apart → mitigate by keeping both maps in the shared theme spec / one source of truth.
- **Risk:** ANSI 256 approximations of "orange" / "white" / "dim" in Herdr may differ slightly from chalk's named colours → verify visually against the CLI.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Pi TUI colouring, sorting changes (WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY), and other Herdr list features are separate work items and must not be expanded into this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope of 'selection list' — should priority-based colours apply to (a) `wl list` / `wl search` / `wl recent`, (b) `wl show` detail view, (c) both?" — Answer (user): "both a and b plus the herdr plugin". Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Priority vs Stage relationship — should priority (a) replace stage as primary colour source, (b) supersede only for title colour keeping stage in metadata, (c) only affect list views?" — Answer (user): "Always use priority in title and stage colouring in id (everywhere they appear)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Blocked items — currently `blocked` is a red override that beats stage. Should blocked items (a) still override everything (always red), (b) show their natural priority colour?" — Answer (user): "b". Meaning: blocked items are coloured by their priority like every other item; the unconditional red override in `renderTitle` is removed. Source: interactive reply.

## Key Files:

- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — import `theme.js` instead of `icons.js`
- `tests/unit/icons.test.ts` — imports move to `theme.ts` (file may be renamed)

- **WL-0MSJ2JFMO007PGQ6** (open, medium) — "Colour code work items by priority in selection lists (CLI + Herdr)". Touches the same `theme.ts` priority/stage maps and herdr colour functions; the shared-source decision for herdr should align with it.

# Intake Brief: Herdr pane title should reflect how it was spawned

## Problem statement

When a pi agent pane is spawned from the Herdr worklist, its title is generic
("Pi Agent" for agent commands, "Command Output" for `!!`/`!` shell commands),
so the user cannot tell at a glance how each pane was spawned or which work
item it belongs to. The downtime dispatcher already names its panes
(`Downtime plan` / `Downtime intake` / `Downtime audit`), but the manual spawn
paths do not.

## Users

- **Herdr users running skill/workflow commands** — want pane titles that
  identify the spawn source (manual vs downtime), the skill invoked, and the
  target work item, so multi-pane sessions are navigable.
  - As a user, I trigger `/skill:implement <id>` from the worklist, and the
    new pane is titled `Manually triggered implement <title> - WL-<id>` so I
    can find it among other panes.
  - As a user running a `!!` shell shortcut (e.g. audit approve/reject), the
    resulting pane identifies the command and work item instead of a generic
    "Command Output".
  - As a user, I see downtime-dispatched panes in the same descriptive format
    so all pi panes follow one naming convention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Agent-command panes spawned from the worklist (skill shortcuts,
   `/intake`, `/plan`) get a descriptive title of the form
   `Manually triggered <skill> <work item title> - <id>`; the skill token is
   derived from the command (e.g. `/skill:implement` → `implement`).
2. Free-form `/prompt:` commands produce a title like
   `Manually triggered prompt <first words…>` (truncated), or a sensible
   fallback when no prompt text remains.
3. `!!`/`!` shell-command panes (routed via `run-in-pane.sh`) get a
   descriptive title instead of the generic "Command Output", identifying the
   command/work item where available.
4. Downtime-dispatched panes are updated from the short `Downtime <kind>` to
   the same full format (e.g. `Downtime triggered <skill> <title> - <id>`),
   keeping one consistent convention across all pi panes.
5. Title length is bounded (truncated) so pane names stay usable in the Herdr
   UI; commands without a work item still get a descriptive-but-safe title.
6. Unit tests cover title construction for each spawn path (manual skill,
   `/prompt:`, `!!`/`!` shell, downtime), including missing work-item and
   missing-title cases.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No change to the interactive `open-pi-agent.sh` pane (keeps "Pi Agent").
- The work-item title must be sourced without adding blocking process spawns
  in the TUI loop — prefer threading the already-loaded item title from the
  worklist state into the spawn path.
- Pane titles must remain safe for herdr pane-rename (no shell metacharacter
  injection; the rename already runs with quoting).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` supports `--pane-name` (default
  `Pi Agent`) and renames the pane after spawning pi.
- Manual agent dispatches go through `buildSendToPiArgs` in
  `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, which does **not** pass `--pane-name` →
  panes are named `Pi Agent`.
- The downtime worker (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) uses
  `buildDowntimePaneArgs` → `--pane-name "Downtime <kind>"`.
- `!!`/`!` shell commands route through `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh`
  which renames the pane `Command Output` (override via `RUN_IN_PANE_NAME`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `resolveAndRouteCommand` has the selected
  item (with `id` + `title`) at dispatch time, but `onCommand` only forwards
  `(command, model)`.

## Desired change

- Extend the agent-command spawn path (`buildSendToPiArgs` call site in
  `index.ts`) to pass `--pane-name` with a title built from a descriptor
  (`Manually triggered`), the skill name parsed from the command, the work
  item title, and the work-item ID.
- Thread the selected item's title from `worklist.ts` into the dispatch
  (extend the `onCommand` seam or pass a prebuilt title) so no extra `wl`
  spawn is needed.
- Add the same `--pane-name` behavior to the `!!`/`!` shell path
  (`run-in-pane.sh` invocation in `index.ts`), replacing "Command Output".
- Update `buildDowntimePaneArgs` / the downtime spawn to the full format so
  downtime panes match (e.g. `Downtime triggered <kind> <title> - <id>`).
- Centralize title construction (descriptor + skill + title + id, with
  truncation) so all spawn paths share one function.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — agent/pane dispatch; add `--pane-name` to
  `buildSendToPiArgs` and the `run-in-pane.sh` spawn.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `resolveAndRouteCommand` / `onCommand`
  seam; forward the selected item's title (or a prebuilt pane title).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `buildDowntimePaneArgs` / pane
  name; adopt the full format (`Downtime triggered …`).
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — pane-name plumbing if the title
  is passed via env/arg.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`
  — tests for the new title construction per spawn path.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9` — "Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item
  and show their status icon". Related: pane spawn plumbing (pane-id capture)
  in the same dispatch path.
- `WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG` — "Allow /skill:audit on complete/in_review items
  without a valid audit". Related: downtime audit tier uses the same
  `buildDowntimePaneArgs` path that will adopt the full title format.
- `WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K` — downtime worker (dispatch panes open in the
  resolved worklog root); pane naming originates here.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the work-item title is threaded from the worklist state
  (already loaded) rather than fetched via `wl show` — avoids extra spawns in
  the TUI loop. If threading proves invasive, fall back to `wl show` at spawn
  (documented tradeoff: extra subprocess per dispatch).
- **Risk:** long work-item titles make pane names unusable — mitigated by
  truncation (bounded length) in the shared title builder.
- **Assumption:** `/prompt:` panes use `Manually triggered prompt <first
  words…>` per user confirmation.
- **Assumption:** `!!`/`!` panes keep the manual descriptor with the command
  and work-item context; exact token order to be confirmed during planning.
- **Scope-creep guard:** interactive `open-pi-agent.sh` naming is explicitly
  out of scope; any further spawn-source descriptors discovered during
  implementation should be recorded as linked work items, not folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which panes should get descriptive titles? (a) Only agent-command
  panes spawned from skill shortcuts (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`,
  `/prompt:`), (b) also the `!!`/`!` shell-command panes (currently
  'Command Output'), (c) also the interactive `open-pi-agent.sh` pane
  (currently 'Pi Agent')?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **b** — agent-command panes AND the
    `!!`/`!` shell-command panes; the interactive open-pi-agent pane is
    excluded.
- Q2: "Should the downtime dispatcher's panes be updated to match the new
  full format (e.g. `Downtime triggered plan <title> - WL-<id>`), or keep its
  current short form (`Downtime plan`) while only the manual path gets the
  descriptive format?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **update** — downtime panes adopt the
    same full format for a single consistent convention.
- Q3: "Free-form `/prompt:` commands have no skill name and may have no
  work-item ID. What should their title be (e.g. `Manually triggered prompt
  <first words…>`), or should they keep the default 'Pi Agent'?"
  - Answer (user, interactive reply): **use the suggested title**
    (`Manually triggered prompt <first words…>`).

## Problem

In the herdr worklog-selection-list plugin, every fetch used by the auto-refresh cycle spawns `wl` via execFile WITHOUT a timeout: `runWl(args)` (fetcher.ts:376) passes `timeout` to execFileAsync only when `timeoutMs !== undefined` (:356), and no caller in the refresh path supplies one (fetchNextItems, fetchItemsByStage, fetchMandatorySubsets, fetchActionableCount). `doRefresh` awaits these inside a `refreshInFlight` single-flight guard (worklist.ts:2497-2503); if a spawn hangs (e.g. waiting on the worklog lock during a long `wl sync`, or a stuck child), the guard stays true forever and EVERY subsequent refresh is skipped — the pane freezes even while focused, with no error surfaced.

Note: runSync (auto-sync.ts:226) already has a 60s spawn safety timeout; the refresh read path does not.

related-to: WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9 (same bug class in the downtime worker path — getNextItem/getNextAuditCandidate in index.ts use direct execFileAsync with no timeout; a single fix adding bounded timeouts to ALL wl spawns would close both).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every wl spawn in the refresh/sync fetch path has a bounded timeout (recommend 30-60s, configurable or aligned with existing constants).
- [ ] A timed-out refresh fails gracefully: toast (`Refresh failed`), guard cleared, next tick retries — never a permanently wedged refreshInFlight.
- [ ] Unit tests: hung execFile resolves to failure after the timeout and the next refresh tick proceeds.

## Suggested approach

Pass a default timeoutMs inside runWl (or runWlInner) when the caller omits one, e.g. `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`, keeping the option to override. Verify no existing tests depend on unbounded spawns.

## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item
